narrative:
The model determined that you have a 43% chance of being a bad credit risk. Because this probability is high enough to cross the bank's approval threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that mattered most in this decision were your savings, the loan amount you requested, and how long you have been employed. Your savings of 1,000 DM or more was the strongest positive factor for you. Having this level of savings (something only 2.9% of approved applicants have) pushed the model strongly toward approving your loan. Unfortunately, the other two important factors worked against you and outweighed that advantage.

The 10,961 DM you asked for is much larger than the average of about 3,020 DM among people who were approved. This large requested amount pushed the prediction noticeably toward bad credit risk. Your employment duration of 4–7 years also pulled the score in the negative direction compared with applicants who have been employed longer.

Taken together, the size of the loan you need and your relatively short time in your current job created too much uncertainty for the bank, even though your solid savings worked in your favor.

You should consider applying again for a smaller loan amount, or wait until you have been with your employer longer so your stability looks stronger. Either change would likely improve your chances.
